Start year.note: Alliant's project page says the plant is expected to be operational in 2030 pending regulatory approval. A Corridor Business Journal article about the commission application says service would start in the second quarter of 2030.

Capacity (MW).note: The Corridor Business Journal article on the commission application says three simple-cycle turbines rated at 240 MW each. This matches GEM.

Equipment Manufacturer/Model.note: A Siemens Energy story from June 2026 says its SGT6-5000F turbines will power the proposed Morgan Valley Energy Center. All three units are the same 240 MW simple-cycle turbine, so the model applies to each. The company's state air permit application, signed July 15, 2026, also lists three Siemens Energy turbines of 240 MW each. It spells the model SCGT6-5000F.

Status Detail.value: July 2026: Interstate Power and Light applied to the Iowa Department of Natural Resources for an air construction permit for three Siemens Energy combustion turbines of 240 MW each. The application gives June 2027 as the date installation on site begins.
Status Detail.note: The permit application gives these facts. No permit has been issued yet.

units.notes: Status stays pre-construction. Alliant has asked the Iowa Utilities Commission for a decision by December 2026 and filed a rezoning request with Linn County in July 2026. The project is moving, so Latest Activity is left alone.

It lists unsited additions, including a combined cycle unit in 2029 that GEM holds as IRP power station 1. A reviewer should decide whether Morgan Valley's 720 MW replaces that placeholder.
qa.note: The plan file is a consultant's comments on the study, not the study itself. No finding here comes from the plan, so the IRP box was not flagged.

qa.recommendation: Keep pre-construction. A commission decision on the certificate is requested by December 2026 and the Linn County rezoning is pending, so construction approval is not yet given.
